0.why: TrigSeqPlus.cpp takes this jack as a rising edge at 1V in Clock mode, and in Cv mode clamps getVoltage() to 0-10V and divides it across the set length

1.why: TrigSeqPlus.cpp compares this jack against 1V, or against -1V when Reverse Input Voltage is set to Negative, at the moment a clock edge arrives

2.why: TrigSeqPlus.cpp compares this jack against 1V as a level, or takes a rising edge when Run Input is set to Trig

3.why: TrigSeqPlus.cpp takes this jack as a rising edge at 1V to jump to the reset step

4.why: TrigSeqPlus.cpp adds this jack's voltage to the STEPS knob, 0-10V covering all sixteen steps

5.why: TrigSeqPlus.cpp reads this jack as a voltage spread across the thirty-two programs, or as a rising edge when Prog Input type is set to Trig

0.why: TrigSeqPlus.cpp writes this port with setVoltage() and there is no setChannels in the file; what it carries depends on Output type and on TURING MODE

comment: The output has no family because TURING MODE changes what it carries: a trigger, gate or clock-width pulse normally, and a stepped control voltage in that mode. The RST knob doubles as the TURING output attenuator, which is why its 1-to-16 configuration is commented out at TrigSeqPlus.cpp:265 in favour of a custom quantity. REV and RST are read only in clock mode, and a reset also sets the program back to 0 when Prog Input type is Trig.
